Content: The developers of Al are inundated with people who are thinking beyond capitalism- thru what it means to develop thoughtful humans who can more readily support multiple ways of thinking, knowing, being. Quantum computing allows for the free movement of resources (human and otherwise).

The resources that were held by so few are released - while much of it was intangible wealth, stocks and bonds were largely dissolved. Communities now have resource models rooted in place - where exchanges, barter, shared economics is prevalent. We learn to value 'the small' much more - the small portions of rice and dal we get to cook and share on biogas stoves after the power goes out, the shoulders we squeeze fleetingly and hands we hold. We learn to practice valuing the life that we have here and now.
Sharing/bartering is primary. Listening ...truly listening to one another is necessary. Stories and wisdom are valued.
We can't always buy every little random thing we want
Post-the abolishing of capitalism, there is an equal distribution of resources. There is a feeling of abundance.
People share, and resources are abundant in an equal way.

Every person has their basic needs met - for food, shelter, medical care, and relationship and belonging. The needs are met through communal care. Profit is no longer a driving motive as all are secure in housing, food, safety, and daily living needs; a safety net exists for catastrophe but is rarely needed. Corporations no longer have rights that equal or exceed people.
Bartered community
Debt is a thing of the past, national debt is erased, student debt, medical debt... what is that? Debt is what you owe another, indebtedness, human to human.

The obscene accumulation of wealth is gone. Our children, born after, don't even realize that there was a time when some had too much. But the human spirit of greed still needs to be tended to. We all need tending to.
Water is no longer something to be owned, bought and sold. Clean and safe water is available to all. (ALSO WATER)

Money still exists - but it is better understood as stored time and energy. We had to rethink banking and large financial systems when the larger financial architecture melted for a few years. It mattered to have regional banks and community financial systems. What mattered most were the relationships - where trust was a premium. One of the most important developments was the practice of mutual aid and giving/sharing/banking systems that extended micro-loans and credit with full dignity and humanity and no ability to prey or inhibit based on what now seem like very outdated modes of keep wealth out of the hands of certain peoples or communities or nations.
We need less - our worth is not measured by how big our house is, or how much status we have through our positionality at work, or as evidenced by a display of wealth.
Private property only exists in small pockets. Networks for skill building and learning are supported - alongside mutual exchange.
We barter and trade a lot.
We've gotten much simpler in how we live and consume energy. No one seems to miss the absence of the many devices and screens.

Books and bookstores have returned and the store doesn't really make sense because nobody uses money anymore. Technology has advanced such that you go there and you read books in slow time in community or the books read themselves to you and there's a way that we can add to the books by adding our oral stories.
We have shed the need to collect more stuff. The weight of property - of ownership has been released as we are cared for and nurtured in our places.
Lack and scarcity are antiquated ideas. Social constructs of identity are leveraged to maximize the fullest potential of global resources.

Less stuff: more relationships and accountability to each other and to our great Mother / More beauty- more flowers / More clothes made out of recycled fabrics from all the clothes in the past-more natural fibres- bringing back the ancestral weavings, and textile traditions, and handmade. We have less clothes but they are beautiful and fit us well and made by people who are treated with dignity and respect/ less plastic based everything / No more single use

Fiat currency no longer existed. Nurtured is the capacity to care for each other, generosity. Ernesto’s work is hosted by an elder and a younger person to develop spiritual and other capacities. Where people learn to use AI and not be used by it.
Wealth is willingly shared and spread out for the good of all.

What was it like working for money? Why did some people hoard resources? Why did the old government impose religion over human rights? Those are questions people ask elders in disbelief but trying to understand history and the past.

There’s equal value in everyone’s work as evidenced by a shared compensation structure (everyone gets “paid” the same throughout their lives), and the collective resources support everyone throughout their whole lives.
The property has minimal value and is transferable
Original of Translation: La propiedad tiene valor mínimo y es transferible.

Content: Everything is free although there is no concept of free. It is whatever people need. Fresh food, water. Provided by the community. Local clinics on every block, everyone has a personal connection with their physician, there is a lot of preventative care. Everyone’s basic needs are met.

No longer the system as we know them. The new system is co-created by everyone. Everyone receives the benefits. Dominance and control are no longer the norm. Equity is. We distribute resources equally. Care for each other. The idea that 1% has the wealth and others have no food is unfathomable.
Capitalism is properly demonized for the flame-out it had been. It’s been sworn off like a bad drug.
Business owners work together to solve each other’s problems because you are trying to work together to make sure everyone succeeds, for the benefit of the community. No businesses fail.
Society shifts in what’s valued and what’s valuable
Wealth distribution, erasure of debt
Prosperity is measured in emotion and resilience, not in physical resources.
Wealth is defined by the richness of relationships. Human connection

We learned from the era of “owning” things and having power over people–of having to stomp on other people to own something.  Mutual understanding and reciprocity.  There are stories told about the tipping points that got us there.
Community central economies.
Open transparent financial system.
Money is not the most important thing, empathy is
Our notions of ‘wealth’ and ‘success’ and ‘prosperity’ are defined by the conditions of all the people around us rather than by our own condition

Eventually, we grew tired of private property. Not because objects and spaces can’t be held close or because there’s not meaning in things we can return to, we can cultivate in our own way and appreciate over and over. We grew tired because we realized common ownership, common shared use creates more care and access and “riches” for all of us.
“Property” (stuff, land, etc.) is communal

Much of what we need is freely available. Free childcare. Two-year maternity leave. Poverty has been eliminated for the last 25 years and there are no differences in health outcomes between various communities! I love my community. I love paying taxes!

Content: We create systems that support life and not productivity for producing sake.

Content: We don’t own as much. We care for with vision to how our future circles will hold and thrive.

Content: We have universal access to skills that keep multiplying resources.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: We value regeneration in all we do.
There is a bartering system.  We trade goods and services with one another.

We will understand that “true gold” doesn’t exist in extraction.  Instead it is in seeing the sacredness of what is in everything.  We will have a deeply renewed relationship to the sacred.  We will see the life that is always hidden inside life.
We don’t need to accumulate.
Plants are huge! Seeds are vital to our existence and will be the currency of bartering and sharing. We are part of the universe and travel in the Universe is available to us.
We have removed the middle man to connection.  Money (or other artificial barriers) are no longer the connection point to the thriving and beauty we already have access to.  We are the connection.
There is basic income for all, people work less. More time for family, home, and interests.
Our economy acknowledges and honors the interdependence of our global ecosystem.

We have removed the ‘’profit motive’’. Corporate greed and profits are no longer more important than people

In the absence of multinational corporations, family farming and self-reliance become increasingly important to survival.
The economy is care-based with many circles of care. It is decided what kind of care is needed.
Money does not exist. Work is not mandated. Everyone has roles according to skill and community need.

Ownership has moved from more individualistic to more collective.  The 99% stewards 99% of the resources.  The 1% concept is lost to history.  Public, collective, and individual are woven seamlessly and stewarded for the benefit of all.
We focus on building the capacity of people’s contributions in this new economic system.

Resources exist and are readily available to all.  We are kind, sharing, and people are embraced rather than othered–everyone gets the help they need connecting to the appropriate resource when needed.  The community gets everyone where they need to go.
There is a highly functional global currency and economy.
People tell the story of how businesses and organizations used to be siloed and confused about what was needed.
In the place of capitalism is a new emerging system that takes value from work in many different forms–balanced for ability.  The focus is on encouraging building capacity and being human centered.
Resources we need are owned and stewarded by all.
Murals and art all around us. Small, thriving businesses with an abundance of locally-sourced products.
People are valued as individuals.
Businesses are deeply rooted in community where barter and other forms of exchange flourish for people’s needs.
The world values people and relationship over profit #nomorecapitalism
Fair pay to cover rent and quality food.

The transition from a money-centered economy, involved a deliberate effort to de-emphasize and place less value money and more value on unique gifts shared and brought to the table by each individual. As a consequence, our thriving future experiences a richness of talent.
Collective prosperity over individual gain.
Enough is the measure of resource distribution on small and large scales.
Descendants of billionaires will be satisfied with enough.
Donut economies.
We’ve given up the game of the infinite seeking of more.
Resources are shared well - with generosity and wisdom. If we grant any status, it is to the person or community that thinks and lives well for the 7th generation ahead.

We’ve given great attention to how goods and services are held in the commons (in public). This has also been the strongest conflict mitigation tool we have. Because the redistribution and sharing of money, food, and buildings sparks good energy and harmony.
We practice financial autonomy at individual, social, regional, and national levels. People freely flow and are well met when they move place to place.

Taki was the village sage. Like  Mbeguida, her wrinkles, stretch marks and moles were tattoos that would invoke envy in the  younger generation, if envy were a quality of character that still existed. Alas, envy in years  before was a result of lack and since every person lived according to her means and  was given according to her needs resources were abundant.

There is no money because we understand that resources are all around us. We’ve created physical spaces such that what we need is at hand. We know how to barter and as a result we greatly respect the resources.

Businesses and unions of the times would understand that a strong union was made of strong families, and that strong families make strong businesses.  The families that work in a business would help each other out, as well as the rest of the community – and everyone would do better.

There will be a thriving Middle Class - Industry will know to invest in long term wellbeing of the community. It’s sustainable.  Businesses will prioritize people working a balanced life.  There will be a healthier workforce.
There are now 5 million systems of currency on Earth, but most people prefer to barter items, services, and information.

Money is useful, but income inequality is limited & managed within acceptable boundaries. People have their basic needs met and thrive in place. “Money” is something that rewards those who perform jobs or design systems that optimize for collective good while minimizing harm. “Owners” or “CEOs” of business are capped in their pay to a 20x multiple of their lowest paid worker.
Jubilee is back!
Universal basic income is implemented worldwide, and work is how people get more but not the necessities (stuff, opportunity, luxury). There are homes for everyone and food available.
No money in the US
All property is public
No need for billionaires. Hoarding wealth is a crime. Billionaires participate in redistribution ceremony to give away their wealth
Money has an expiration date
The ones we most respect are not the ones who have the most but those who have given the most away
Love is valued higher than the dollar <3
Only collective ownership exists for the good of all and the earth (no profit)
You win by having the least, not the mosT!
No one gets in trouble for being poor
No one is poor
We don’t see anything as being “just ours” anymore.  The idea of mine is super uncommon.  We don’t own anything.  It is everyone's.

No billionaires in our system – money (or whatever currency) needs to be distributed not hoarded. Instead of currency, people trade labor or resources or just simply share and practice mutual aid. In order to work, employers are required to provide wellness benefits to employees and make rest a priority.

No production, industries or professions. Humanity adopts generalism, with allowance to pursue passions. Tech and AI and automation focused on sustaining and maintaining, not “growth” or “profit.” We can pursue our creativity and passions while contributing to an ecosystem that sustains our collective livelihood.

A smaller world, without borders, where people communicate with a lot of love and affection. People have a lot of wisdom and do not need much to live. Richer is the one who needs the least. People live happily.
Original of Translation: Un mundo más pequeño, sin fronteras, donde la gente se comunica con mucho amor y cariño. La gente tiene mucha sabiduría y no necesita mucho para vivir. Es más rico el que menos nececita. La gente vive feliz.

Content: Workers own the means of production, the land, the factories.
Communism replaces capitalism in a way which has never done before.  People live communally and share almost everything.
Because we  no longer work to earn a paycheck and make or not make profits for an employer, we now work to live a balanced life. So start by being responsible to our selves for ourselves.
Billionaires don’t exist. Open trade worldwide.

Early on we seized the means of production and began to redistribute extreme wealth (the top 1%). We then found our way into bartering and then a gift-based economy. We wear ethically sourced high-quality clothes that are made to last.  In fact, we were able to reverse the phenomenon of ‘’planned obsolescence’ and instead build things with meaningful durability. We changed our relationship to the material world. We are happy with much less. It’s not about stuff, but about living well, and honoring the origins of what we create. There are strict regulations on how large companies operate and the imperative is to benefit the community. We’ve removed profit motives and GREED is not rewarded. Science is about problem solving and learning and not finding profitable products and drugs.
Flow with our resources; public good & "individ-well"
The West provides more, takes away much less from other countries.

Communities are not worried about resources. There will be enough for our folks. No work is looked down upon – we restored a pursuit of taking care of oneself and finding personal passions (did I mention that all AI generated art forms have to now be labeled as AI generated art?). All labor is seen as equally valuable in creating a working, safe, stable society where all are fairly compensated: a regenerative style of supporting each other is embedded into our economic system.
As a community, we practice bartering where we exchange our produce without using money.
Wealth is distributed.
Orange County is flourishing as the safe and modern town to live. People need money, but not for food or healthcare, mostly for other things, like things that bring joy.
